title: Directive Signal Sprint
content:
Goal:
- Rapidly iterate a small library of directive-style prompts that make model outputs reliably follow structural signals (sections, bullet semantics, action items).
- Focus on 3 axes: explicit section markers, example-driven patterns (few-shot), and negative instructions that deter undesired formats.

Context / why: 
- Prod customers have had regressions when we roll new tokenizers/quantization profiles where models ignore delimiters or collapse bullets. Need patterns that are resilient across model variants and small context shifts.
- This is a personal sprint log: quick experiments, hypotheses, and failure traces to feed into a shared kit later.

High-level hypothesis: 
- Combining 2 strong examples (few-shot) with an initial explicit delimiter and a short schema statement reduces format-errors by ~40% vs single-shot.

Mini-plan (today -> next week):
1) Build 6 prompt templates: 3 sectioned ("---SECTION---" style), 2 explicit schema lines, 1 example-heavy few-shot.
2) Evaluate on 120 samples (varied instruction fluency + token budgets 60/160/512).
3) Log failure modes and craft negative-instruction counterexamples.
4) Push top-2 templates to shared drive and open a PR for small nudge in SDK examples.

Prompt templates (working drafts):
A) Structural delimiter + schema
"You are an assistant that must output ONLY the sections below. Start with ===BEGIN=== and end with ===END===.
SCHEMA:
- SUMMARY: one sentence
- ACTIONS: numbered list of atomic steps
- NOTES: short bullets (if any)

User: {{instruction}}
"

B) Two-shot strong examples (compact)
"Below are two examples showing the exact format. Match them exactly (including punctuation).

Example 1:
SUMMARY: The user needs a quick checklist to deploy.
ACTIONS:
1) Build container
2) Push image
3) Update deployment
NOTES:
- Keep secrets in KMS

Example 2:
SUMMARY: The user needs a rollback plan.
ACTIONS:
1) Revert manifest
2) Scale down new pods
NOTES:
- Monitor errors for 5m

User request: {{instruction}}
"

C) Negative instruction + compact schema
"Do NOT include explanations or extra context. If information is missing, state 'MISSING: <field>'. Output must contain: SUMMARY, ACTIONS.
User: {{instruction}}
"

Few-shot data ideas (for seeding):
- Ops requests: rollout, rollback, hotfix notes (40)
- Product tasks: release checklist, feature flagging steps (40)
- Support replies: triage steps for incidents (40)

Quick evaluation rubric (manual + automated):
- Structural pass (automated regex): has SUMMARY, ACTIONS section and ends with newline.
- Fidelity: human-rated 1..5 (does the ACTIONS map to the instruction?)
- Conciseness: token length vs ideal (target trim threshold).
- Hallucination indicator: mentions resources not in prompt (human audit).

Failure cases observed (notes from quick runs):
- Model drops numbered bullets when token budget within 30 tokens of limit (collapse to a single paragraph).
- Model pads NOTES with generic filler like "- none" even when relevant details exist.
- With few-shot, model sometimes literalizes example content (repeats exact example text) rather than adapting.
- Negative instruction sometimes flips: model refuses to answer citing policy (odd classifier trigger).

Raw trace snippets (for debugging):
- Input (C template) short: "Create rollback plan" -> Output: "SUMMARY: MISSING: context ACTIONS: 1 rollback 2 monitor NOTES: - none" (collapsed bullets, missing granularity)
- Input (B template) with two-shot -> Output: repeated Example 2 unchanged then appended "User requested: Create rollback plan" (failure to adapt)

Hypothesized fixes to try (ranked):
1) Increase few-shot example diversity and avoid reusing exact phrase anchors (swap synonyms).
2) Add explicit instruction: 'Do not repeat examples verbatim; adapt wording to the user request.'
3) Add a short post-formatting instruction asking for numbered bullets only: 'Use Arabic numerals and put one action per line.'
4) If token budget low, prefer schema compression (use short keys like S:, A: instead of full words).

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Templates A/B/C x budgets [60,160,512] x 3 model variants (small/medium/large) x 2 negative-instruction toggles = 54 runs per sample set.

Metrics capture plan:
- CSV with columns: prompt_id, template, budget, model, sample_id, structural_pass, fidelity_score, tokens_out, notes.
- Local script: save examples/outputs to /tmp/dir-sprint-asha (todo: move into shared drive).

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Generate 120 seed instructions (split across ops/product/support). (Diego assigned)
- [ ] Implement regex structural_pass script (Maya)
- [ ] Run matrix on small model for quick feedback (Asha)
- [ ] Collate failures and craft 6 counterexamples for the negative-instruction set (All)
- [ ] Draft short Confluence page with results and recommended template (after experiments)

Notes to self: 
- Keep prompts compact; every extra sentence increases chance of format bleed.
- Watch out for privacy: some seeds include internal config names; scrub before sharing.
- When adding to SDK examples, include a small 'gotcha' note about token budgets.

References / links:
- Linear ticket: RED-4821 (variance in format outputs)
- Past drives: shared_drives/product/hosted-api/prompt-guides (need to cross-check)

Questions unresolved: 
- Is there an existing small-model baseline with the new tokenizer? (ask infra)
- Does Redwood SDK handle output post-processing in examples today? If so, how much should we rely on it vs instructing model to be precise?

If I get 1 hour: prepare the 120 seeds and run template A @ 160 tokens on small model, capture top 20 failures.
If I get a full day: run the full matrix on small/medium and summarize with top 10 recurring failure signatures.

End notes: 
- This doc is intentionally informal. Will migrate polished templates to shared_drives once stable.
- Keep snapshots of raw model outputs for regression detection.
